claim: Conservative Q-Learning (CQL) is proven to be 'gap-expanding': at large enough regularization strength, the learned Q-function widens (never narrows or inverts) the gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution action values relative to the true gap.
stance_target: a provable, positive property distinguishing well-behaved pessimistic value/acquisition functions from ones that invert real-vs-invented rankings
scope_conditions: Offline Q-learning with the CQL regularizer, for large enough alpha (the tradeoff coefficient)
quoted_support: "Theorem 3.4 (CQL is gap-expanding). At any iteration k, CQL expands the difference in expected Q-values under the behavior policy pi_beta(a|s) and mu_k... for large enough values of alpha_k"

claim: Prior offline RL methods that do not explicitly constrain or regularize the Q-function may fail to be gap-expanding, allowing out-of-distribution actions to have higher learned values than the true gap would justify.
stance_target: the assumption that any offline value/surrogate estimator is automatically conservative toward out-of-distribution points
scope_conditions: Standard (unregularized) offline Q-learning methods, contrasted empirically in the paper's Appendix B
quoted_support: "When function approximation or sampling error makes OOD actions have higher learned Q-values, CQL backups are expected to be more robust... prior offline RL methods that do not explicitly constrain or regularize the Q-function may not enjoy such robustness properties."

claim: CQL produces a provable lower bound on the true value of the current policy for a sufficiently large regularization coefficient, and this coefficient can be made smaller as the offline dataset grows.
stance_target: background context for CQL's conservative-value-estimation framing
scope_conditions: Continuous control (SAC-based) and discrete control (QR-DQN-based) offline RL settings
quoted_support: "as increases, the theoretical value of alpha that is needed to guarantee a lower bound decreases, which indicates that in the limit of infinite data, a lower bound can be obtained by using extremely small"
